# Buffered depth: proposed interface and normalization obligations

This is a research interface, not an OC proof. Defect and Slab are writing
and independently auditing the fixed-body core and fixed-face cover.
Statements below distinguish their checked identities from the remaining
outer-variation problem.

## 1. Why change the depth regions

Unqualified active-normal KKT is false at an actual deepest point, as the
triangle frustum shows. First-order neutrality also need not continue a
deepest point. Instead alter the depth functional itself by a controlled
small amount while preserving convexity of its superlevel regions.

For a canonical hull of finitely many positive d-dimensional fibers, let
f(z,x) be a nonnegative jointly concave fiber functional, continuous on
the hull and zero at each fiber boundary. Initially fix a norm G on the
continuous covectors. Define

 b_e(z,x)=min{pure-base closed depth at z,
   inf_(a,u:G(u)=1) mu{a.(Z-z)+u.(X-x)>=-e f(z,x)}}.

With c_q(a,u)=sup{c:mu{a.Z+u.X>=c}>=q}, its superlevel constraints are

    a.z+u.x-e f(z,x)<=c_q(a,u).

They are convex constraints because f is concave. Original fiber sums
are retained. Uniform continuous strip bounds yield b_0<=b_e<=b_0+O(e)
on the compact original set. The constants depend on the fixed family
and norm, not on base tilts. The exact scope, attainment, quantile plateau
orientation and extension to a compact class are being written separately.

## 2. The natural projective power

The particularly useful choice is f=E^(1/(d+1)). Joint concavity follows
from the proved concavity of E^(1/d) and the increasing concave power
d/(d+1). At an interior mark the energy envelope formula gives

    grad_x f=f a_opt.

For a regular active buffered cap with G(u)=1, unrestricted normal
stationarity gives the mixed section centroid

    (p, y-e f grad G(u)).

Its exact source balance is sum rho_j u_j=e grad_x f, with positive
normalized rho. In Euclidean normalization this is the displaced-centroid
identity previously found by root; arbitrary fixed smooth norms replace
u by grad G(u) only in the section centroid.

Under the LOCAL source-fiber projective change v'=v/(1+a_opt.v), a cap
u_j.v>=-e f becomes

    (u_j-e f a_opt).v'>=-e f.

These transformed continuous normals have weighted sum zero. This is
only algebra on the one ordinary fiber. Applying the projective change
to the entire mixed measure would change integer labels and is forbidden.

If (alpha,f a_opt) is a joint supergradient, then

    L=1+(alpha/f).(z-p)+a_opt.(x-y)>=1/(d+1)

on the entire canonical hull, by the existing positive energy-chart
theorem and the differentiable power rule. Thus the projective parameter,
critical continuous normal balance and globally positive chart now agree.
The base resultant sum rho_j a_j-e alpha supports the buffered deepest-
base hull. This is the new interface; it does not establish mass payment.

## 3. Fixed faces and nested changes

Given a joint supergradient extending the source balance, weighting the
active constraints shows that every deepest base lies on the nonpositive
side of that corrected base resultant. Its equality face contains the
source's minimal deepest-base face. On that face the weighted actual cap
margin is at least e f(z,x). Consequently those actual caps cover each
whole actual fiber there, although they need not cover its entire
continuous plane.

If the body shrinks, the UNNORMALIZED energy power is monotone at fixed
marks. With the old norm and parameter fixed, holding the weighted sum
of cap thresholds fixed therefore preserves the BUFFERED cover on those
fixed faces. This supplies a possible analogue of the old parity-witness
cover for nested deformations. It is not an outward-variation theorem.

Updating the supporting threshold to exploit an energy derivative must
retain ALL maximizers of the old supporting affine gap over the face.
The derivative at one selected mark is insufficient to certify a cover
of every other contact fiber. This obligation is separate from the
single-source stationarity identity.

## 4. Affine normalization is a separate issue

Unnormalized f=E^(1/(d+1)) scales with degree d/(d+1) under continuous
homothety, and a fixed Euclidean covector norm is not invariant under a
general continuous GL transformation. A minimum over a canonically
normalized compact family cannot therefore be treated as an unrestricted
shape minimum for this functional without additional work.

A candidate fully invariant version uses

    f=(E/M)^(1/(d+1)),
    Sigma=(1/M)sum_z |K_z| Cov_uniform(K_z),
    G_C(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u).

Sigma is positive definite for positive full-dimensional fibers. It
ignores translations of individual fibers and transforms as A Sigma A^T
under a common continuous GL map A. Therefore the corresponding buffered
cap condition is invariant under continuous GL maps, translations and
affine continuous shears depending on the base. These operations preserve
the mixed lattice and scale all fiber masses by the same determinant.

For a fixed body this is just a fixed ellipsoidal norm and the same
projective gradient identity. Under a BODY VARIATION, however, both M
and Sigma change. The response includes the normalization derivative of
f and the additional term e f G'_C(u). They cannot be omitted. Moreover
normalized f need not decrease under a nested change, so the elementary
nested-cover argument in Section3 does not transfer unchanged.

Either a fixed-frame outer minimization with properly tracked normalization,
or an invariant variation theorem retaining these extra terms, remains
necessary. No new global extremizer or descent is assumed here.

## 5. Completed interface update, Registry121

The former existence and normalization obligations are now proved in
`candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb`, with independent
Slab audit PASS. No normalized-buffer restriction is needed: original
bad-minor minimality compactifies the whole original bad sublevel, which
contains every buffered bad minimizing sequence. All valid normalization
maps preserve the buffered functional. Uniform properness is chosen before
minimizing; limiting energies, covariances and all cap depths are controlled.

`candidate c6bafe9ff5de0861`
provides the exact updated-normalization continuation for arbitrary nearby
compatible paths. The minimum over ALL old integer contact marks provides
the correct threshold budget. Under its signed radial and regular-cap
hypotheses the response includes energy, total mass and covariance. the contributor
and Defect audits PASS. A separate all-status supporting inverse is under
audit; it must not be replaced by arbitrary facet allocations.

The occupied-parity rigid-stratum theorem now pays all buffered deepest
fibers, but not the others. Full witness saturation removes multiple-contact
minima and also removes anchored relations among those witnesses themselves.
Thus the substantive new mathematical obligation is a physical inequality
or structural classification at an attained bad minimum that keeps the
outside fibers. The existing proved interface does not resolve that claim.
